- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and model shows gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., >10/30d) and sentiment is bearish, model should underpredict sharp drops; adjust downward bias by 5–10% of recent range.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast rise at 5–7% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is bullish but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 65), reduce forecast slope to avoid overbought bias.  
- When official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model should not assume “recovery” — forecast should lag true drop by 1–2 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67) and model is trending upward, check for recent supply events — if supply is high, reduce forecast slope by 10–15%.  
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative sentiment, apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in “recovery” narratives.
